source: Measured axis: Monnier et al. (2012), ApJL 761, L3, inclination 6.2 ± 0.4 degrees from the line of sight and pole position angle -58 ± 6 degrees east of north (source/photometry/gravity-darkening.json), the pole tilted toward us; computed by inclinedPoleOrientation in tools/objects/observation/gravity-darkening.mts.
coordinateSystem: ICRF/J2000. +Z is the measured rotation pole, the one tilted toward the Earth. +X is the display meridian, set so that grid longitude 0 faces the Sun and Earth at the scene epoch; east longitude. No spin is propagated: the surface has no longitude features to show it.
qualification: The pole direction is measured by interferometric imaging (Monnier et al. (2012), ApJL 761, L3). The spin phase and prime meridian are a display convention; the rotation is not animated.
